correctness.rationale: Headline computations replay correctly from committed edge lists: deletion-contraction polynomials for all 8 graphs re-ran byte-identical in audit (independent brute-force q^n coloring-count interpolation also matches G1/G2/G4; wheel closed-form P(W_n)=q*((q-2)^(n-1)+(-1)^(n-1)*(q-2)) matches G2/G3/G6 exactly); structural identities (monic deg n, coeff n-1 = -m, P(0)=P(1)=0, sum 0) hold; P(2)/P(3)/((-1)^n P(-1)) values verified; Matrix-Tree counts verified for G1/G2/G4/G5 (384/841/3528/1805) with one-edge tau splits summing correctly; ao brute-force 2^m verified for G1/G2 (1862/2184); exact-rational Sturm replay confirms cube V(2)=V(3)=3 with P(2)=2/P(3)=114 nonzero and total distinct real roots 2 (so only 0,1), and antiprism brackets [643/256,645/256] and [871/256,873/256] each with strict sign change + Sturm drop exactly 1 + P'>0 at both ends and P' Sturm count 0 inside (simplicity), gap (645/256,871/256] count 1, total distinct real 6 consistent with 0,1,2,3,r1,r2. 3-connectivity verified by pair-removal. BUT as stated the draft is false on two essential reporting points: (1) Sec.1/8 claims all 8 committed integer straight-line embeddings are crossing-free and 86 checks pass — audit exact segment test finds 0 crossings for G1-G7 but 10 disjoint-edge crossings/touches for G8 (apex (2,2)-(0,0) diagonal passes through (1,1)=vertex 5, etc.; vertex-on-nonincident-edge degeneracy), so G8 polyhedral membership is not established by the committed evidence (graph is in fact planar, but certificate invalid); (2) Sec.3 recorded one-edge DC splits contradict artifacts/results.json while both sum correctly, e.g. G1 tau 276+108 vs json 160+224, ao 1318+544 vs 1172+690; same mismatch pattern for G2-G8 (all sums match, components differ, no edge identifier given), so the logged splits are unverifiable/inconsistent. verify.py also hardcodes an absolute research-workspace path, so `python3 artifacts/verify.py` does not replay from the committed inputs as claimed. Headline Theorems 1-2 survive, but class-membership and split-log claims fail as written.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison shows the table is recomputation, not a new result. Six of eight polynomials are textbook: wheels G2/G3/G6 follow the classical closed form (verified byte-identical above); cube G1 and prisms G5/G7 are standard examples with published transfer-matrix/deletion-contraction formulas (Read/Biggs; prism family). General Tutte identities T(1,1)=trees, ao=(-1)^n P(-1) are Backman survey theory, and Matrix-Tree/brute-force agreements instantiate rather than extend it. Shrock-Xu gives infinite-family Tutte-ratio asymptotics near tau+1, Royle gives (1,2) counterexamples for 3-connected graphs, Harvey-Royle resolves B10 existence — none records this 8-graph fragment, but that absence does not establish priority: the per-graph values are direct evaluations of prior formulas/methods on named classical graphs. The genuinely per-graph content (cube [2,3] root-freeness; antiprism r1/r2 brackets) is an immediate corollary of the (known or instantly computable) polynomial via exact Sturm evaluation, i.e. a new certificate format for an old/mechanically-computable value, not a substantively distinct claim. No source was found tabulating the square-antiprism/capped-prism polynomials with these brackets (arXiv chromatic+antiprism query returns 0 hits), but a failed search does not establish priority, and the method (memoized deletion-contraction + Sturm) is the standard textbook procedure applied to another 8-vertex graph.

value.rationale: Even taken as new, the fragment is not independently worth retrieving. The eight graphs are acknowledged as `classical polyhedral representatives, not an exhaustive census' — an arbitrary finite slice with no extremality, completeness, or downstream theorem. Cube [2,3] root-freeness follows trivially from its classical polynomial (P(2)=2, P(3)=114) and answers no open zero-freeness question (Royle's (1,2) failure is for non-bipartite 3-connected graphs; cube is bipartite). The two antiprism brackets are certified enclosures with only numerical Beraha proximity (r1 within 0.107 of B5, r2 within 0.012 of B8), explicitly `not a limit/accumulation/exact-equality claim' — i.e. unexplained numbers: no accumulation theorem, no equality to a Beraha number, no general criterion, no already-used downstream fact. Per the shared standard, certification alone does not rescue an arbitrary object or an unexplained number, and a rigorously established narrow datum passes only when the value was not known/mechanically implied and a future researcher could need the precise fact; here wheel/cube/prism values are known by formula, and no reason is given why a future Birkhoff-Lewis/Jackson/Sokal/Beraha user would need these particular brackets versus any other small polyhedral graph. Honest incompleteness does not erase a headline, but there is no independently valuable exact headline — only recomputed polynomials plus two proximate real roots with no mathematical interpretation.
